халқаро аэропорти}}}} {{Airport codes|TAS|UZTT}} is the main [[international airport]] in [[Uzbekistan]], the second busiest airport in [[Central Asia]] (after [[Almaty International Airport]] in [[Kazakhstan]]), and [[List of the busiest airports in the former Soviet Union|the 7th busiest airport in the former Soviet Union]]. It is located {{convert|12|km|nmi|frac=2|abbr=off}} from the center of [[Tashkent]]. It was named after [[Islam Karimov]], the first [[President of Uzbekistan|president of independent Uzbekistan]] from 1991 to 2016. Construction of a New Tashkent International Airport[https://www.gazeta.uz/ru/2026/05/05/new-tashkent-airport/ Строительство аэропорта «Новый Ташкент» планируется начать в июне] is currently underway in the [[Oʻrtachirchiq District|Oʻrtachirchiq]] and [[Quyichirchiq District|Quyichirchiq]] districts of the [[Tashkent Region]], 7 km from [[Yangiyoʻl]]. The airport is scheduled to open in late 2030. Following its completion, the existing Islam Karimov Tashkent International Airport is slated to close.[https://uzbuild.uz/ru/news/novyj-aeroport-taskenta-postroat-v-7-km-k-vostoku-ot-angiula-lokacia Новый аэропорт Ташкента построят в 7 км к востоку от Янгиюля][https://daryo.uz/ru/hAuiST-DR/ Новый аэропорт Ташкента построят с участием трех стран. Работы начнутся уже в июне][https://www.uzdaily.uz/ru/podpisano-soglashenie-o-gchp-po-stroitelstvu-novogo-aeroporta-tashkenta/ Подписано соглашение о ГЧП по строительству нового аэропорта Ташкента] {{cite web |url=https://jp.ibtimes.com/sojitz-joins-226-billion-tashkent-airport-project-103213|title=Sojitz joins $2.26 billion Tashkent airport project}} == History == [[File:The Trans Asian Express first operated in November 1967, flying Copenhagen Moscow Tashkent Bangkok Singapore. Pictured is a stopover in Tashkent in the Soviet Union.jpg|thumb|left|Douglas DC-8 of Scandinavian Airlines pictured during a stopover in Tashkent in the [[Uzbek SSR]]]] The history of Tashkent Airport dates back to the early 20th century. On 12 May 1924, the first passenger flight was completed on a Junkers R-13 aircraft along the Tashkent–[[Pishpek]]–[[Almaty]] route.{{cite news |url=https://kun.uz/kr/18739340 |title=The ancient air terminal of Central Asia – History of Tashkent airport |date=9 March 2024}} On 8 August 1930, the first airlift connected Moscow with Tashkent. The first Moscow-Tashkent-Moscow flight was operated on a [[Kalinin K-4|K-4 aircraft]].{{Cite web|url=https://tashtrans.uz/2017/05/23/istoriya-razvitiya-grazhdanskoj-aviacii-v-uzbekistane/|title=История развития гражданской авиации в Узбекистане}} In 1957, the [[Tu-104]] jet aircraft began operating on the Moscow-Tashkent-Moscow route. This was preceded by a radical upgrade of the radar and communication services. New landing systems, RSP-4, were introduced in Tashkent. Then, the Romashka radar system was deployed. In 1958, Tashkent Airport was granted the status of an international airport of Class I. In 1967, the [[Yakovlev Yak-40]] and [[T-34 variants]] aircraft were introduced. The capital of Uzbekistan was connected by direct air links with [[Saint Petersburg]], [[Novosibirsk]], [[Sverdlovsk, Ukraine]], [[Chelyabinsk]], [[Simferopol]], cities of the [[Baltic states]], the [[Caucasus]], and the [[Far East]]. On 20 September 1972,{{Cite web|url=https://ria.ru/20131231/987461353.html|title=Сверхзвуковой авиалайнер Ту-144: летно-технические характеристики - РИА Новости, 01.03.2020}} the supersonic [[Tu-144]] aircraft made its first flight on the [[Moscow]]-[[Tashkent]]-Moscow route.{{Cite web|url=https://fishki.net/2178928-31-dekabrja-1968-goda-sovershil-pervyj-v-mire-polet-sverhzvukovoj-passazhirskij-samolet-tu-144.html|title=31 декабря 1968 года совершил первый в мире полет сверхзвуковой|date=30 December 2016|website=fishki.net}} The cruising speed of the airliner reached {{Convert|2500|km/h||abbr=on}}, and it covered the distance from Moscow to Tashkent in 1 hour and 50 minutes. [[File:Tashkent Airport, 1980s uzbekistan.jpg|thumb|left|A picture of Tashkent Airport in the 1980s]] === Independent Uzbekistan === [[File:Uzbekistan Airways Ilyushin Il-62 Wallner-1.jpg|thumb|left|Uzbekistan Airways Ilyushin [[Il-62M]] aircraft at Tashkent International Airport]] On 28 January 1992, [[Uzbekistan Airways]] was established.{{Cite web|url=https://www.uzairways.com/ru/press-center/news/trete-voskresene-avgusta-den-vozdushnogo-flota-uzbekistana|title=Новости | Официальный сайт АО "Uzbekistan Airways"|date=9 June 2025|website=www.uzairways.com}} In the same year, the airline, under its [[Airline codes|code]] HY, operated its first international flight from [[Tashkent]] to [[London]] on an [[Il-62]] aircraft.{{Cite web|url=https://podrobno.uz/cat/obchestvo/natsionalnaya-aviakompaniya-uzbekistan-airways-prazdnuet-svoe-28-letie/|title=Национальная авиакомпания Uzbekistan Airways празднует свое 28-летие|website=Podrobno.uz}} In 1993, the airport served 1,409,900 passengers. During the mid-1990s, significant renovations were carried out with the help of Western construction companies.{{citation needed|date=December 2024}} This ICAO Category II airport is the primary [[airline hub|hub]] of [[Uzbekistan Airways]], the largest international airport in Uzbekistan, and the busiest in Central Asia. The airport comprises two terminals: Terminal 2 receives international flights, and Terminal 3 is for domestic traffic.{{cite news |title=Uzbekistan Airways' new terminal starts operation in Tashkent |url=http://www.caan.asia/en/show-uzbekistan_airways%E2%80%99_new_terminal_starts_operation_in_tashkent.html |access-date=26 September 2011 |newspaper=C.A.A.N |date=26 September 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150213161244/http://caan.asia/en/show-uzbekistan_airways%e2%80%99_new_terminal_starts_operation_in_tashkent.html |archive-date=13 February 2015 |url-status=live}} In March 1995, Uzbekistan Airways started flights from Tashkent to [[New York City]] via [[Riga]]. It used [[Airbus A310]]s on the route.{{cite news | url=https://www.uzdaily.uz/en/post/31750 | title=Uzbekistan Airways marks 20th anniversary of launch flights to New York | work=UzDaily | date=3 April 2015 | accessdate=12 January 2023}}{{cite journal | id={{ProQuest|224308831}} | title=World airline report: 1994 - Europe | journal=Air Transport World | volume=32 | issue=6 | date=June 1995}}{{cite news | url=https://rus.delfi.lv/biznes/bnews/riga-privlekaet-aviakompanii.d?id=9441083 | title=Рига привлекает авиакомпании | work=Biznes & Baltiya | date=1 November 2004 | accessdate=13 May 2023 | author=Novak, Alexey | language=ru}} Terminal 2 was rebuilt in 2001, and renovations were completed in 2018. It has a capacity of 1000 passengers/hour and serves more than two million passengers per year. Facilities include waiting lounges, CIP and VIP halls, restaurants and bars, currency exchange offices, duty-free shops, airlines ticket counters and sales offices, and a 24-hour pharmacy.{{citation needed|date=May 2026}} [[File:Boeing 757-200 at Tashkent airport.jpg|thumb|Uzbekistan Airways Boeing 757-200 at Tashkent International Airport]] Terminal 3 opened in 2011 with a capacity of 400 passengers per hour. The two terminals are separated by the runway, requiring passengers transiting from international to domestic flights and vice versa to exit the airport in order to transfer between them.{{citation needed|date=March 2023}} In July 2017, Uzbekistan Airways began offering nonstop service to New York using its Boeing 787 fleet.{{cite news | id={{ProQuest|1923950367}} | title=Uzbekistan Airways conducts first non-stop Tashkent-New York-Tashkent flight | work=UzDaily | date=28 July 2017}}{{cite web | url=https://www.uzairways.com/en/our-story | title=Our story | work=Uzbekistan Airways | accessdate=12 January 2023}} [[File:TAS A.P. International duty free shop 2023.9.29.jpg|thumb|Tashkent International Airport [[duty-free]] shops]] On 25 January 2017, the airport was named after Uzbekistan's First President, [[Islam Karimov]].{{cite web |title=Об увековечении памяти Первого Президента Республики Узбекистан Ислама Абдуганиевича Каримова |url=http://uza.uz/ru/documents/ob-uvekovechenii-pamyati-pervogo-prezidenta-respubliki-uzbek-25-01-2017/ |access-date=1 April 2017 |archive-date=18 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170518112619/http://uza.uz/ru/documents/ob-uvekovechenii-pamyati-pervogo-prezidenta-respubliki-uzbek-25-01-2017 |date=25 January 2017 |language=ru |trans-title=On perpetuating the memory of the First President of the Republic of Uzbekistan Islam Abduganievich Karimov}} === Expansion === Since 2021, the area of the international terminal at Tashkent International Airport has expanded by nearly 50%, growing from {{Convert|45000 to 65000|m2||0|abbr=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.spot.uz/ru/2024/09/04/airport-reconstruction/|title=К 2026 году планируется объединить залы прилета и вылета аэропорта Ташкента|date=4 September 2024|website=Spot – Деловые новости Узбекистана}} In August 2024, another stage of building expansion was completed at Tashkent International Airport's terminal. Large-scale reconstruction works included the renovation of the facade, the departure hall, and the waiting areas for passengers and visitors. A drop-off zone for passengers was added near the entrance, allowing vehicles to approach the first floor. A new hall for passengers and those seeing them off was also introduced, along with a small green recreation area equipped with benches. The airport also began testing a passenger monitoring system called Pax Track.{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazeta.uz/ru/2024/08/31/tashkent-airport-reconstruction/|title=Фото. Как изменился международный аэропорт Ташкента: отсутствие забора, Pax Track и другое – Новости Узбекистана}}{{Cite web|url=https://anhor.uz/news/pax-track/|title=В аэропорту столицы запущена система Pax Track|date=31 August 2024|website=Anhor.uz}}{{Cite web|url=https://weproject.media/articles/detail/chto-novogo-poyavilos-v-tashkente-v-2024-godu-kak-izmenilas-stolitsa-uzbekistana/|title=Что нового появилось в Ташкенте в 2024 году — как изменилась столица Узбекистана|website=weproject.media}} In November 2024, Tashkent International Airport began an expansion of its arrival hall. The terminal's façade will be extended forward, increasing the area nearly twofold. The expansion will allow for the addition of two baggage carousels and a new area for meet-and-greet services inside the building. The arrival hall's area is set to increase by {{Convert|2500|m2||0|abbr=}}, expanding from the original {{Convert|5300|m2||0}}. The project is slated to be completed by May 2025, with the final phase involving the merger of the departure and arrival terminals. This will create a unified airport complex with a capacity to handle 2,400 passengers per hour.{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazeta.uz/ru/2024/11/20/airport/|title=Началась реконструкция зала прилёта международного аэропорта «Ташкент»|date=20 November 2024}} In 2024, the airport served 8.7 million passengers, which is 28% more than the previous year's results. It is the busiest airport in Uzbekistan as well as [[List of the busiest airports in the former Soviet Union|the 7th busiest in the former Soviet Union]].{{citation needed|date=May 2026}} By 2026, the airport plans to merge its arrival and departure terminals. == Facilities == [[File:20230607 khiva019.jpg|thumb|[[Boeing 787]] of [[Uzbekistan Airways]] in Tashkent International Airport]] [[File:Tashkent International Airport backlight.jpg|thumb|Tashkent International Airport control tower]] Covering an area of {{Convert|100|ha||abbr=on}}, it includes 110 parking spaces for aircraft and features two [[runway]]s: northern and southern — both of which meet international standards for accommodating large aircraft, including [[Boeing 787]] and [[Airbus A380]] models.{{citation needed|date=January 2026}} Runway 08L/26R with an asphalt surface, measuring {{Convert|4000|m||0|abbr=}} in length and {{Convert|60|m||0|abbr=}} in width. Runway 08R/26L, also with an asphalt surface, is {{Convert|3905|m||abbr=}} long and {{Convert|45|m||0|abbr=}} wide.{{citation needed|date=January 2026}} Inside the terminal building, 56 monitors are installed to display information for passengers. An electronic ticketing system is also in place.{{cite news |title=Tashkent International Airport to Be Modernized |url=http://daryo.uz/2015/05/01/toshkent-xalqaro-aeroporti-modernizatsiya-qilinadi/ |access-date=26 March 2016 |archive-date=14 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414065019/http://daryo.uz/2015/05/01/toshkent-xalqaro-aeroporti-modernizatsiya-qilinadi/ }} Since 2024, a 24-room hotel for passengers has been operational at Tashkent International Airport.{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazeta.uz/ru/2024/01/29/airport-hotel/|title=В международном аэропорту Ташкента открылся отель для пассажиров (+ фото)|language=ru|website=Газета.uz|date=29 January 2024|access-date=17 March 2024}} == Services == {{unreferenced section|date=May 2026}} [[File:20230616 002 Tashkent airport.jpg|thumb|Towing tractors at Tashkent International Airport]] The airport is equipped with a variety of vehicles for technical services, including Mulag Comet and [[Nissan]] towing tractors, Hunnert Gmbh water dispensers, [[Mitsubishi Fuso Rosa]] passenger buses, and Alfons Cak fuel dispensers. == Airlines and destinations == [[File:Ил-114 в аэропорту - panoramio.jpg|thumb|[[Ilyushin Il-114]] of [[Uzbekistan Airways]] at Tashkent International Airport]] [[File:20230616 011 Tashkent airport.jpg|thumb|[[Turkish Airlines]] [[Airbus A330-200]] at Tashkent International Airport]] The airport is considered one of the largest and most modern airports in [[Central Asia]]. It offers services for numerous aircraft and passengers, along with a variety of service facilities. Due to its advantageous location, it facilitates flights to [[Europe]], [[Southeast Asia]], the [[United States]]. Tashkent International Airport is the hub for [[Uzbekistan Airways]], the national carrier of Uzbekistan, which operates an extensive network of direct flights to numerous destinations. The airport serves several other international airlines that connect Tashkent with destinations primarily in the [[Commonwealth of Independent States|CIS]] region. [[Turkish Airlines]] also has a significant presence at the airport, with 14 weekly flights from Istanbul, making it the airline with the second-highest number of weekly flights after [[Uzbekistan Islam Karimov Tashkent International Airport (IATA: TAS, ICAO: UZTT) is the main international airport in Uzbekistan, the second busiest airport in Central Asia (after Almaty International Airport in Kazakhstan), and the 7th busiest airport in the former Soviet Union. It is located 12 kilometres (6+1⁄2 nautical miles) from the center of Tashkent. It was named after Islam Karimov, the first president of independent Uzbekistan from 1991 to 2016.
Construction of a New Tashkent International Airport is currently underway in the Oʻrtachirchiq and Quyichirchiq districts of the Tashkent Region, 7 km from Yangiyoʻl. The airport is scheduled to open in late 2030. Following its completion, the existing Islam Karimov Tashkent International Airport is slated to close.
